title: Fix bookmark paging and add tag filter
intent: Users can page through all of their bookmarks and narrow the list to one tag.
problem_statement: GET /bookmarks drops items when paging: the reported symptom (45 bookmarks do not add up across pages) points to an off-by-one in the page window. Fix it so pages are contiguous and complete, and add an optional, case-insensitive tag filter applied before paging, without changing the response for existing clients that do not send a tag.

acceptance_criteria.text: Paging through GET /bookmarks returns every bookmark exactly once; a full page has exactly `size` items.
GET /bookmarks?tag=<t> returns only bookmarks having tag t, matched case-insensitively and exactly (not substring).
With a tag filter, `total` counts matching bookmarks and paging applies to the filtered list.
Requests without `tag` behave exactly as before (backward compatible); invalid paging values still return 422.
Regression tests cover the paging bug; docs/api.md documents the tag filter.

non_functional: No breaking change to the response shape
Filtering cost is linear in stored bookmarks (in-memory store)

ambiguities.question: Should `?tag=py` match `python` (substring) or only `py`?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: Substring matching returns surprising results and cannot use an index later.

ambiguities.question: Should multiple tags (`?tag=a&tag=b`) be supported?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: AND vs OR semantics would need a decision.
ambiguities.assumption: Single tag only for now; out of scope.
